findings.evidence: "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month. A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day" (monthly), but "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year" (annual)
findings.fix: Clarify whether the equipment catalog is updated monthly or annually, and revise conflicting statements to use consistent terminology.
findings.violation: The equipment catalog update frequency is contradictory - the program overview indicates monthly updates, but later sections only reference annual fiscal-year publication.

findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year" and "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back"
findings.fix: Specify whether returning employees receive a fresh stipend allocation or whether their claim limit remains based on their original benefit year.
findings.violation: It is unclear whether an employee returning from approved leave receives a new stipend claim or continues within their existing benefit year, creating ambiguity around the "one claim per benefit year" limit.

findings.evidence: "an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives"
findings.fix: Clarify whether "missing item" refers to missing documentation and specify what action the requester must take to resolve the pause.
findings.violation: "Missing item" is ambiguous - it could refer to missing documentation (receipt) or missing equipment information, creating confusion about what must arrive to resume processing.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Revise to consistent voice, such as "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the company may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first sentence
findings.violation: The sentence mixes employee voice ("you") with employer voice ("we"), creating an inconsistent tone.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee"
findings.fix: Either list the equipment categories explicitly or reference where employees can find the complete list.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second sentence
findings.violation: The term "categories" is referenced but never defined in the document, leaving employees uncertain about what counts as a distinct category.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form" versus earlier statement "Employees start a stipend request in the benefits portal"
findings.fix: Clarify that all requests are submitted through the benefits portal (or revise to use consistent terminology) and remove references to a separate request form.
findings.location: Terminology Notes section, first two sentences
findings.violation: It is unclear whether "request form" and "benefits portal" refer to the same process or two different processes.

findings.evidence: "Stipend item" is used repeatedly - "You record the stipend item," "Finance reconciles the stipend item," "Payroll releases the stipend item amount" - without definition
findings.fix: Define "stipend item" clearly at the start of the Terminology Notes section (for example: "A stipend item is a single piece of equipment included in a stipend request").
findings.violation: The term "stipend item" is undefined; it is unclear whether it refers to each individual piece of equipment or the total monetary amount being claimed.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt" versus the detailed three-step process in "How to Apply" (start request, save draft automatically, review confirmation summary)
findings.fix: Either expand this section to match the complete process described in "How to Apply" or delete it to avoid duplication and confusion.
findings.violation: This section presents an incomplete and contradictory summary of the request process compared to the fuller explanation earlier in the document.

findings.evidence: Section titled "Special Cases" contains only routine information about equipment catalog publication at fiscal year start
findings.fix: Rename the section to reflect its actual content (such as "Equipment Catalog Publication") or populate it with actual special cases.
findings.violation: The heading promises special cases or exceptions but the section content does not deliver on this promise - it merely repeats standard procedural information.
